extracted.intended_audience: authors of accepted manuscripts for Acta Mathematica / contributors preparing final accepted LaTeX submissions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors who have had a paper accepted at Acta Mathematica on how to prepare and submit the final manuscript (LaTeX source, figures, abstract, bibliography) for print and web presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability: accepted manuscripts only
rubrics_metrics.description: These instructions are for accepted manuscripts only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note! These instructions apply only after acceptance; follow them when preparing the final version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript preparation: style and layout
rubrics_metrics.description: Please consult a recent issue of Acta Mathematica to get a general idea of the style and layout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should conform to the journal's style and layout. Changes other than typographical must be approved by the editor in charge. When revising your manuscript take these author instructions into consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval required for non-typographical changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that changes other than typographical must be approved by the editor in charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make substantive edits without prior approval from the responsible editor; contact the editor if substantive changes are necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography completeness and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: We are quite careful with the bibliography. We therefore ask you to fill in any missing data in the reference list, update the references as much as possible, and delete any reference that is not relevant to the current version of your paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure every reference has full bibliographic data, update items where appropriate, and remove obsolete or irrelevant references before final submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colour figures: printing and greyscale visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Acta Mathematica is printed in black and white. If you wish to have figures printed in colour, you have to be prepared to contribute to the extra cost. In the online version colour figures will appear free of charge. If you have colour figures that will be printed in black and white it is important that they are clearly visible in greyscale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare figures so they remain clear when converted to greyscale; expect to pay for color printing if required; online color has no extra charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirement and web presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Please make sure that your paper begins with an abstract. The abstract will not be printed, but it will be used on the web. Each paper in Acta Mathematica is presented with abstract and bibliography on the web.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an abstract at the start of the manuscript for web presentation even though it will not appear in the printed journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: File naming convention
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of the TeX file should be the surname of the (first) author with the extension .tex. If the surname has more than eight letters, use only the first eight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name the main .tex file as specified to ease editorial handling (first author's surname, max eight letters, with .tex extension).

rubrics_metrics.name: File preparation: include macros and EPS figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Any macros and non-standard style files should be included. Figures should be submitted separately as encapsulated postscript (.eps) files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Package all non-standard .sty/.cls and macro files with your submission; supply figures as separate .eps files (encapsulated PostScript).

rubrics_metrics.name: File transfer / submission system
rubrics_metrics.description: All files are handled through EditFlow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload all files via the EditFlow system. For further questions contact acta@mittag-leffler.se.
